candidates.tagline: They look just like regular sunglasses — and that's the whole problem
candidates.story: Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses are so well-designed to blend in that bystanders can't tell they're being filmed; singer Lorde told a Meta-sponsored Madrid festival crowd in July 2026 'don't get the glasses — they are not sexy,' and Meta has since added an Instagram ban for glasses-enabled harassment after public backlash.
candidates.why_funny: The glasses succeeded perfectly at looking like normal sunglasses — which is exactly why everyone is outraged. They worked as designed.
candidates.alt: Black Ray-Ban Wayfarer-style smart glasses resting in front of their tan leather charging case, indistinguishable from regular sunglasses with no visible camera

candidates.tagline: Apple hid the Mac mini power button on the BOTTOM — 'people hardly use it'
candidates.story: Apple's Mac mini M4 (launched late 2024) has its power button recessed on the underside of the device, requiring users to flip their computer upside-down to press it; Apple defended the choice saying users 'hardly ever' need the physical button, until macOS 26.5 added a keyboard shortcut workaround in May 2026.
candidates.why_funny: Apple charged up to 1,399 USD for a desktop computer and hid the on/off button where no one can see or reach it without turning the whole machine upside-down — then justified this by saying nobody uses it anyway.
candidates.alt: Apple Mac mini M4 desktop computer photographed at an angle showing its front USB-C ports and the bottom face of the device, where the power button is hidden from normal view
